summary: This article explains how Wangari Maathai of Kenya started the Green Belt Movement, which trained women to plant tens of millions of trees, and became the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.
introduce: Write Inform, Persuade, and Entertain on the board and give a one-line example of each. Tell students to decide, while reading “Wangari Maathai and the Green Belt”, which purpose the writer had and to find one sentence that proves it.

keyTerms.def: a very young plant that has just grown from a seed
the slow wearing away of soil or rock by water or wind
wood that is burned to cook food or keep warm

challengeTerms.def: a person who works to protect the natural world
the highest degree a university gives, earned after years of advanced study and research
able to continue for a long time without using up or harming natural resources

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that one person can make a big difference for the environment? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how planting trees helped both the land and the women of Kenya.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review seedling, erosion, and firewood, and let weak readers underline sentences that inform and circle any that persuade.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use environmentalist, doctorate, and sustainable in a short paragraph that explains the writer's purpose and how the details support it.
